html:
A people from western Asia, probably from the Levant, who settled in the eastern Nile Delta and ruled northern Egypt as its Fifteenth Dynasty, from about 1650 to 1550 BCE. The name comes from Egyptian words meaning "rulers of foreign lands".

They did not arrive in one sudden invasion. Settlers from Canaan had been growing in number in the Delta for generations, and as the Middle Kingdom broke down their leaders took power. They ruled from Avaris, a large city with Canaanite houses, temples and burials, while native kings held Thebes in the south. The Hyksos king Apepi courted an alliance with Kerma in Nubia against Thebes.

Egypt probably gained the horse and chariot and new kinds of bronze weapons in this period. The Theban king Ahmose I drove the Hyksos out around 1550 BCE and took Avaris, founding the New Kingdom. Later writers, including the Jewish historian Josephus, linked their expulsion to the story of the Exodus.
